died: c. 1556, Lavra de la Trinidad-San Sergio, Sergiev Posad (Rusia)
language: Greek (writings in Greek and Latin-humanist formation; Slavonic/Russian in Moscow)
role_place: Greek humanist monk: Dominican house of San Marco, Florence, c. 1504–1506 (per en.wikipedia); Vatopedi (Athos) from 1507; Moscow from 1518 at the request of Vasily III; condemned at councils of 1525 and 1531, imprisoned/exiled until 1551–1553.
why_relevant: One of the few 16th-century Orthodox writers with a dedicated doctrinal polemic against Muhammad and the Qur'an (two discourses plus an answer to Muslim attacks on Christianity).
fame: Known mainly as a translator, humanist and reformer of Russian religious books; canonised 6 June 1988 by the Local Council of the Russian Orthodox Church (per en.wikipedia). His anti-Islamic writings are far less cited than his translation work. The English Wikipedia article does not mention Islam at all (checked).
orthodox_status: saint (canonised 1988, Russian Orthodox Church); monk, translator, theologian
team_note: Before returning to Orthodoxy at Athos in 1507 he was in a Dominican house in Florence (c. 1504–1506). The works quoted here are later (before 1525), so they are Orthodox. Orchestrator to confirm this fits the brief's exclusion rule.
